flaws: In the low-angle view, the wooden saddle brackets atop the vertical support pillars do not actually touch the underside of the track—there is a clear air gap beneath the middle and right-side supports, leaving the ramps floating.
In the close-up view of the cup, the dark blue catch-box walls intersect and clip directly through the white cup geometry, and the end of the light-wood ramp clips awkwardly into the front blue wall.
In the top and low views, the far-left base of the marble run and its tall starting pillar overhang off the left edge of the desk surface into thin air rather than sitting cleanly on the tabletop.
The dark blue deflector panels at the mid-track turn and around the cup are thick, blocky slabs that obscure the target cup and clash with the delicate brass-and-wood aesthetic.
parsed.summary: The marble run achieves 100% reliability (16/16 trials) and features a charming brass-and-wood desk toy aesthetic with nice desk props, but it falls short of a 9+ due to floating support brackets, overhanging base geometry on the left, and severe mesh clipping around the target cup.
